Workers connect to iii over WebSocket and register functions and trigger types. Registry installs
and local source use separate, explicit surfaces.

## Registry package

```bash
iii worker add state@next
```

`iii worker add` accepts only a Registry reference. It resolves a normalized PackageDescriptor,
verifies its digest, writes the descriptor and immutable artifacts to `iii.lock`, and executes that
descriptor.

## Local Compose catalog

Declare local source under the root `workers` map and select it from a stack as
`catalog://<slug>`. Registry-backed stack entries use `package://<slug>@<version-or-channel>`.

```yaml
workers: {}
stacks:
  default:
    namespace: dev
    containers:
      state:
        worker: package://state@next
```

```bash
iii compose validate --file worker-compose.yaml --stack default
iii compose --up --file worker-compose.yaml
```

Stacks cannot define scripts, environment, working directories, or artifact versions separately.
Those fields belong to the compiled PackageDescriptor.
